brands.name: Tanner Surfboards
brands.short_description: Hand-shaped longboards, gliders, hulls, and mid-lengths from Tanner Prairie in Costa Mesa — classic California logging and alternative craft.

models.name: Baby
models.description: Inspired by Phil Edwards and his balsa board he called “baby”. This model trims and turns with ease. The outline is sleek and overall rocker is flat. The 60/40 rails provide control and flow through turns. Works best in waves 2-6 feet. Recommended fin - baby glass on or Quigg speed fin

models.name: Mike Rogers Model
models.description: The Mike Rogers model is a design Tanner and Mike have been working on for over 10 years. It has a very balanced outline and foil. It is a great all around board and daily rider. Works great in a variety of waves from 2-3 foot blackies to 6-8 foot Newport Point. Best with a Greenough style flex fin.

models.name: Dirty Martini
models.description: Levi Prairie signature model. Great all around log with a pulled in nose. Really loose and jivey in the pocket. Enhances style and subtle flair. Flat rocker overall and pinched 50/50 rails. Works best in 2-4 foot waves.

models.name: Gliders
models.description: Inspired by Skip Frye. This style board is meant to harness the beauty and simplicity of riding waves. Around 11 foot in length these boards glide into waves with ease. They like to trim in the pocket and the length encourages smooth turns. There are so many different variations of gliders from the classic pintail, to a long fish shape. Really fun in a variety of waves from 2-6 feet. Works well with a variety of fin set ups.

models.name: Dash
models.description: Inspired by the "malibu chip" board from the 1950's. This board is a modern take on a classic era. The original outline was pulled off a Mike Marshall board shaped for Kio aka Yellow Rat. This design encourages in the pocket traditional surfing and finding the perfect trim. Works best in clean logging waves and point breaks. Overall flat rocker and neutral bottom with 60/40 rails. Works best with a 8.5" Quigg speed fin.

models.name: Luna
models.description: Luna is my take on the traditional noserider. Nose concave, parallel rail, wide point aft of center, and tail kick work simultaneously to provide lift and a steady platform when on the nose. Everything is blended in a way to not compromise trim when on the center of the board. Take a step back and the tail kick allows you to pivot from rail to rail. Works best in 2-4 foot waves.

models.name: Paisley
models.description: This pintail egg is a really fun all around board. It catches waves easily and gets up to trim even on smaller waves. Works well in 3-6 foot waves. Can be customized with different fin configurations.

models.name: Standard Hull
models.description: If effortless speed and down the line trim is what your after then this is the board. Inspired by Greg Liddle. This board works well in point waves and clean, lined up beach breaks. Smooth plane shape, pinched rails, hull entry and "s" deck are what give this board its unique characteristics. It is very different than conventional style boards so there is a bit of a learning curve. It encourages a more front foot style turning. The feeling you get when drawing out a big bottom turn and locking into trim is like no other. Works best with a volan flex fin.

models.name: Flower
models.description: This model is a cross between a vee bottom and a hull. Yet it's more user friendly than both. It excels in point waves and clean beach breaks. Hull entry, neutral bottom, and rolled vee in the tail. Catches waves easy. My favorite size is 8'4". Works best with a flex fin.

models.name: Scout
models.description: The scout model is a glider design inspired by Skip Frye. It works well in a variety of conditions in waves 2 to 6 foot. It has a slight rolled entry to single concave in the center, blended to a double concave in front of the fin to vee out the tail. The edge in the tail helps give it some bite in the turns. I recommend a 8.5" flex fin.
